Hi Leah — thanks for sending this over and for the call. We can meet the timeline but want to ensure the technical evidence is accurate. High-level answers below; we will attach a control-mapping workbook and the most recent SOC 2 Type II shortly.

Quick answers:
- SOC 2 scope: Our SOC 2 Type II report covers the Redwood hosted API and the Redwood Dedicated offering (reserved capacity) — details and scoping notes are in the SOC report we will link. Private/on-prem installs have a separate control boundary; we can provide a SOC addendum and technical checklist for private deployments.
- Data residency (hosted): customer data for hosted tenants is stored in region-specific object storage; we do not replicate across regions by default unless customer configures cross-region backup. We will supply the region-by-region persistence matrix.
- BYOK / KMS: For Redwood Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via integrations with AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For hosted API customers, we offer HSM-backed tenant keys for enterprise plans; BYOK for hosted customers is available via an add-on and we can outline the technical handshake.

Next steps we propose:
1) We will return the completed SIG workbook with a control mapping column (Redwood control reference + artifact link) by EOD Thursday (2026-03-05).
2) Vivek (security) will drop the control mapping spreadsheet and a redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF for legal.
3) If TelcoOne needs a deeper session on KMS integration, Neha can demo the Dedicated/Private key flows.

I have cc'd Neha (SE) and Vivek (Security) to own the technical responses and evidence. Let me know if splitting the SIG by domain is helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Leah / team — attaching the control mapping workbook (Redwood_control_mapping_TelcoOne.xlsx). The sheet maps each SIG question to Redwood's internal control ID, the evidence artifact we can provide, and any redaction/limit notes. Summary highlights below: 

- SOC 2 Type II: attached redacted copy (link included in related_links). The report covers hosted API and Dedicated; private installations are out of scope but we provide configuration checklists. Redacted items remove customer-specific identifiers and internal IPs.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for object storage and LMK-managed keys in our HSMs for tenant encryption by default. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-supplied KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Evidence: config snapshots (s3-encryption-policy-2025-12.txt), KMS integration runbook (KM-Runbook-v3.pdf).
- Access control / identity: we provide role-based access control across services, SCIM for customer SSO, and audit logs forwarded to customer-controlled endpoints for Dedicated. Evidence: access-review-samples.pdf, scim-integration-guide.pdf.
- Change control / deployment: can provide change tickets and release notes (internal trace IDs redacted) covering the last 6 months. Evidence: change-log-extracts.zip (metadata list included in workbook).

Note on attachments: some artifacts contain internal IPs and trace IDs; we've redacted those fields and documented redaction in the workbook. If TelcoOne requires unredacted artifacts for an on-prem review, we can provision a secure share after an NDA/TOE.

Action items we will deliver by EOD Thursday (2026-03-05):
- Completed SIG workbook with control mapping (Redwood_control_mapping_TelcoOne.xlsx)
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II PDF (SOC2-2025-type2-redacted.pdf) and evidence index
- KMS integration summary and BYOK procedure doc for Dedicated/Private

If you want the attachments staged in a secure S3 share or via DocuSign envelope for signature, tell me which method your legal/procurement prefers.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
